## Author's thesis (paraphrased from source)

The document is a common form, with its instructions, by which a software producer attests that the software it produces is developed in conformity with specified secure software development practices (p. 2) [AP]. Its stated purpose is "to provide the Federal Government assurances that software used by agencies is securely developed" [V] (p. 1). It identifies "the minimum secure software development requirements a software producer must meet, and attest to meeting, before software subject to the requirements of M-22-18 and M-23-16 may be used by Federal agencies" [V] (p. 2).

Its background section sets out, in turn, FISMA, which authorises the OMB Director to promulgate information security standards; Executive Order 14028, which required NIST to issue guidance on software supply chain practices and the OMB Director to ensure agencies comply with it; and OMB Memorandum M-22-18 as amended by M-23-16, under which an agency may use software subject to M-22-18 only if its producer has first attested to compliance with practices "drawn from the SSDF" [V] (pp. 1–2) [BT]. The form says it "fulfills the minimum requirements set forth by OMB" [V] in M-22-18 as amended by M-23-16 (p. 4).

In Section III the signer attests that, to the best of their knowledge, the producer "presently makes consistent use" [V] of four practices derived from the SSDF: development and build in secure environments, secured by six listed actions at a minimum; a good-faith effort to maintain trusted source code supply chains; provenance for internal code and third-party components; and automated tools or comparable processes that check for security vulnerabilities, with three further conditions (pp. 6–7) [AP]. The signer further attests that the producer will notify every agency it has submitted the form to if and when it stops making consistent use of those practices (p. 7) [AP]. An appendix maps each requirement to a subsection of E.O. 14028 and to related SSDF practices and tasks, a mapping "provided for reference purposes" [V] (p. 9).

The form must be signed by the producer's CEO or a designee who is an employee with authority to bind the corporation (p. 4) [AP]. The instructions give two other routes. The producer may instead submit a third-party assessment by a qualifying Third Party Assessor Organization (3PAO), in which case it need not sign; and where an agency cannot obtain a completed self-attestation, it may still decide to use the software if the producer identifies the practices it cannot attest to, documents the practices it has in place to mitigate the associated risks, and submits a plan of actions and milestones (POA&M), with the agency responsible for requesting an extension or waiver from OMB (p. 4) [AP].

## Part I: Authority and purpose (pp. 1–2)

### Privacy Act Statement (p. 1)

A bracketed note says this Privacy Act Statement is unique to DHS: all agencies using "this common form" [V] will need to provide an agency-unique Privacy Act Statement when they request to use it, and each should provide statements that conform to its own agency procedures and requirements (p. 1) [AP]. The authority for the collection is given as 44 U.S.C. § 3554, E.O. 14028, "Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity", and OMB Memorandum M-22-18 as amended by M-23-16 (p. 1) [BT]. Under Purpose: "The purpose of this form is to provide the Federal Government assurances that software used by agencies is securely developed." [V] (p. 1).

Under Background, the information may be disclosed as generally permitted under E.O. 14028 and M-22-18 as amended, and, for DHS, as authorised by the routine uses published in DHS/ALL-002, Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Mailing and Other List System, November 25, 2008, 73 FR 71659 (p. 1) [BT]. "This form collects contact information from vendor employees who make the attestation." [V] (p. 1).

The statement names two consequences. "Failure to provide any of the information requested may result in the agency no longer utilizing the software at issue." [V] And: "Willfully providing false or misleading information may constitute a violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001, a criminal statute." [V] (p. 1).

### FISMA, E.O. 14028 and M-22-18 (p. 2)

FISMA, the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014, requires each Federal agency to provide security protections for both "information collected or maintained by or on behalf of an agency" [V] and "information systems used or operated by an agency or by a contractor of an agency or other organization on behalf of an agency" [V] (p. 2) [BT]. FISMA and other provisions of Federal law authorise the Director of OMB to promulgate information security standards, including to ensure compliance with standards promulgated by NIST (p. 2) [BT].

E.O. 14028, "Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity", emphasises the importance of securing the software the Federal Government uses to perform its critical functions, and required NIST to issue guidance "identifying practices that enhance the security of the software supply chain" [V] (p. 2; footnote 1 cites E.O. 14028, Section 4(e)) [BT]. The NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) (SP 800-218) and the NIST Software Supply Chain Security Guidance, "taken together" [V], are referred to in the form as "NIST Guidance", and they "include a set of practices that create the foundation for developing secure software" [V] (p. 2) [BT].

E.O. 14028 further requires the OMB Director to take appropriate steps to ensure that Federal agencies comply with NIST Guidance; to that end OMB issued M-22-18, "Enhancing the Security of the Software Supply Chain through Secure Software Development Practices", on September 14, 2022, and updated it on June 9, 2023, through M-23-16 (p. 2) [BT]. M-22-18 as amended "provides that a Federal agency may use software subject to M-22-18's requirements only if the producer of that software has first attested to compliance with Federal Government-specified secure software development practices drawn from the SSDF" [V] (p. 2) [BT].

### What the form is for (p. 2)

"This self-attestation form identifies the minimum secure software development requirements a software producer must meet, and attest to meeting, before software subject to the requirements of M-22-18 and M-23-16 may be used by Federal agencies." [V] (p. 2). Software producers use it to attest that the software they produce is developed in conformity with specified secure software development practices (p. 2) [AP].

## Part II: Which software needs an attestation (pp. 2–3, 5)

### Three conditions (pp. 2–3)

"Software requires self-attestation if any of the conditions is met:" [V] (p. 2)

1. "The software was developed after September 14, 2022" [V] (p. 2).
2. "The software was developed prior to September 14, 2022, but was modified by major version changes" [V] after September 14, 2022; the form's parenthetical example reads "e.g., using a semantic versioning schema of Major.Minor.Patch, the software version number goes from 2.5 to 3.0" [V] (p. 2).
3. "The producer delivers continuous changes to the software code (as is the case for software-as-a-service products or other products using continuous delivery/continuous deployment)" [V] (p. 3).

### Categories not in scope (p. 3; repeated p. 5)

"Software products and components in the following categories are not in scope for M-22-18, as amended by M-23-16, and do not require a self-attestation:" [V] (p. 3)

1. "Software developed by Federal agencies" [V] (p. 3).
2. "Open-source software that is freely and directly obtained by a Federal agency" [V] (p. 3).
3. "Third-party open source and proprietary components that are incorporated into the software end product used by the agency" [V] (p. 3).
4. "Software that is freely obtained and publicly available" [V] (p. 3).

Section I of the form repeats the four categories as what, for the specified software, "this form does not cover" [V], applying them to "software or any components of that software" [V] in those categories (p. 5). Its second item reads "Open source software that is freely and directly obtained directly by a Federal agency" [V] (p. 5).

### Third-party components and the producer's own code (pp. 3, 5)

Software producers who use third-party components in their software "are required to attest that they have taken specific steps" [V], detailed in Section III, Attestation and Signature, of the common form, "to minimize the risks of relying on such components in their products" [V] (p. 3). Section I adds a note: "In signing this attestation, software producers are attesting to adhering to the secure software development practices outlined in Section III for code developed by the producer." [V] (p. 5).

### Future versions (p. 5, footnote 4)

Footnote 4 sits on the Version Number column of Section I's product table: "Attestations are binding for future versions of the named software product unless and until the software producer notifies the agencies to which it previously submitted the form that its development practices no longer conform to the required elements specified in the attestation." [V] (p. 5).

## Part III: Completing and submitting the form (p. 3)

### Agency-specific additions (p. 3)

"Agency-specific instructions may be provided to the software producer outside of this common form." [V] (p. 3). Conformance to agency-specific requirements "may be included with this form as an addendum" [V], and agencies are responsible for fulfilling any Paperwork Reduction Act requirements that apply to agency-specific additions (p. 3) [AP].

### Submission routes (p. 3)

The instructions give two routes, Online Form Instructions (selecting the URL https://softwaresecurity.cisa.gov) or Local PDF Instructions (p. 3) [AP]. "If a software producer is unable to submit via the online form, they may email a pdf version of the form to the respective agency" [V] (p. 3). A completed form saved as a PDF is named for the software producer, the complete product name, the version number and the attestation date, in the pattern `[Software Producer]_[Product]_[Version]_[Attestation Date]`, with the example `Acme_SecuritySuite_4.6.2.1_20230124` (p. 3) [AE]. "Individual agencies will provide their respective email addresses." [V] (p. 3).

### Completing the form (p. 3)

Under Software Producer Information, the producer is asked for a description of the software and information about the producer (p. 3) [AP]. "All fields in the attestation form are required to be appropriately completed by the software producer. Incomplete forms will not be accepted." [V] (p. 3).

## Part IV: Who signs, and the alternatives (p. 4)

### The signer (p. 4)

"The form must be signed by the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the software producer or their designee, who must be an employee of the software producer and have the authority to bind the corporation." [V] (p. 4). "By signing, that individual attests that the software in question is developed in conformity with the secure software development practices delineated within this form." [V] (p. 4). The software may be used by a federal agency, consistent with M-22-18 as amended, "once the agency has received an appropriately signed copy of the attestation form" [V] (p. 4).

### Third-party assessment (p. 4)

"The software producer may choose to demonstrate conformance with the minimum requirements by submitting a third-party assessment documenting that conformance." [V] (p. 4). The conditions, in the form's words (p. 4):

- "A third-party assessment must be performed by a Third Party Assessor Organization" [V], abbreviated 3PAO, "that has either been FedRAMP certified or approved in writing by an appropriate agency official" [V].
- "The 3PAO must use relevant NIST Guidance that includes all elements outlined in this form as part of the assessment baseline." [V]
- "To rely upon a third-party assessment, the software producer must check the appropriate box in Section III and attach the assessment to the form." [V]
- "The producer need not sign the form in this instance." [V]
- "The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure that the assessment is not posted publicly, either by the vendor or by the agency itself." [V]

The Section III statement the producer checks for this route is recorded in Part VI (p. 7).

### When no attestation can be obtained: POA&M, extension or waiver (p. 4)

Under Additional Information: "In the event that an agency cannot obtain a completed self-attestation from the software producer, an agency may still decide to use the producer's software if the producer identifies the practices to which they cannot attest, documents practices they have in place to mitigate associated risks, and submits a plan of actions and milestones (POA&M) to the agency." [V] (p. 4). The producer's part has three elements: identifying the practices it cannot attest to, documenting the practices in place to mitigate the associated risks, and submitting a POA&M to the agency (p. 4) [AP]. "When an attestation is not provided, per OMB guidance, agencies are responsible for requesting from OMB an extension or waiver for the continued use." [V] (p. 4). Section I's status checkboxes include "Attestation Following Extension or Waiver" (p. 5) [AP].

### Status of the form (p. 4)

"This common self-attestation form fulfills the minimum requirements set forth by OMB" [V] in M-22-18, as amended by M-23-16 (p. 4). "The attestation form, background, and instructions are subject to change and may be modified." [V] (p. 4).

## Part V: The form, Sections I and II (pp. 5–6)

### Section I: status, type and products (p. 5)

The form is headed "Secure Software Development Attestation Form" and "Version 1.0" (p. 5). Section I offers three status checkboxes (New Attestation; Attestation Following Extension or Waiver; Revised Attestation) and three for Type of Attestation (Company-wide; Individual Product; Multiple Products or Specific Product Version(s), with a request for a complete list) (p. 5) [AP]. "If this attestation is for an individual product or multiple products, provide the software name, version number, and release/publish date to which this attestation applies." [V] (p. 5). The product table's columns are Product(s) Name, Version Number (if applicable, carrying footnote 4) and Release/Publish Date (if applicable); "Additional pages can be attached to this attestation if more lines are needed" [V] (p. 5). Section I then lists the four categories the form does not cover and the note on code developed by the producer (Part II above) (p. 5).

### Section II: producer and contact (pp. 5–6)

1. Software Producer Information: Company Name, Address, City, State or Province, Postal Code, Country, Company Website (pp. 5–6) [AP].
2. "Primary Contact for this Document and Related Information (may be an individual, role, or group)" [V]: Name, Title, Address, Phone Number, and Email Address, which "may be an alias/distribution list" [V] (p. 6).

## Part VI: Section III, the attestation requirements (pp. 6–7)

### The attestation statement (p. 6)

"On behalf of the above-specified company, I attest that, to the best of my knowledge, [software producer] presently makes consistent use of the following practices, derived from the secure software development framework (SSDF)" [V], "in developing the software identified in Section I" [V] (p. 6). Footnote 5: "The SSDF are standards and best practices established by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-218." [V] (p. 6).

### Practice 1: secure development and build environments (pp. 6–7)

- **1.** "The software is developed and built in secure environments. Those environments are secured by the following actions, at a minimum:" [V] (p. 6)
- **1a.** "Separating and protecting each environment involved in developing and building software;" [V] (p. 6)
- **1b.** "Regularly logging, monitoring, and auditing trust relationships used for authorization and access:" [V], with two objects, (i) "to any software development and build environments" [V] and (ii) "among components within each environment" [V] (p. 6)
- **1c.** "Enforcing multi-factor authentication and conditional access across the environments relevant to developing and building software in a manner that minimizes security risk;" [V] (p. 6)
- **1d.** "Taking consistent and reasonable steps to document, as well as minimize use or inclusion of software products that create undue risk within the environments used to develop and build software;" [V] (pp. 6–7)
- **1e.** "Encrypting sensitive data, such as credentials, to the extent practicable and based on risk;" [V] (p. 7)
- **1f.** "Implementing defensive cybersecurity practices, including continuous monitoring of operations and alerts and, as necessary, responding to suspected and confirmed cyber incidents;" [V] (p. 7)

### Practice 2: trusted source code supply chains (p. 7)

- **2.** "The software producer makes a good-faith effort to maintain trusted source code supply chains by employing automated tools or comparable processes to address the security of internal code and third-party components and manage related vulnerabilities;" [V] (p. 7)

### Practice 3: provenance (p. 7)

- **3.** "The software producer maintains provenance for internal code and third-party components incorporated into the software to the greatest extent feasible;" [V] (p. 7)

### Practice 4: checking for security vulnerabilities (p. 7)

- **4.** "The software producer employs automated tools or comparable processes that check for security vulnerabilities. In addition:" [V] (p. 7)
- **4a.** "The software producer operates these processes on an ongoing basis and prior to product, version, or update releases;" [V] (p. 7)
- **4b.** "The software producer has a policy or process to address discovered security vulnerabilities prior to product release; and" [V] (p. 7)
- **4c.** "The software producer operates a vulnerability disclosure program and accepts, reviews, and addresses disclosed software vulnerabilities in a timely fashion and according to any timelines specified in the vulnerability disclosure program or applicable policies." [V] (p. 7)

### The further attestation: notifying agencies (p. 7)

"I further attest that the software producer will notify any agency to which it has submitted this form if and when the producer ceases to make consistent use of the practices identified above in developing the software." [V] (p. 7). See also footnote 4 on future versions (p. 5), in Part II.

### Signature, or third-party assessment (p. 7)

The signature block is labelled "Signature of CEO or Designee with authority to bind the corporation" [V], followed by Date (YYYY-MM-DD), Name and Title (p. 7). Below it, after "OR", is the statement for the third-party route. It opens "A certified FedRAMP Third Party Assessor Organization" [V], then the abbreviation 3PAO in parentheses, and continues: "or other 3PAO approved in writing by an appropriate agency official has evaluated our conformance to all elements in this form. The 3PAO used relevant NIST Guidance that includes all elements outlined in this form as the assessment baseline. The assessment is attached." [V] (p. 7). Section III closes with ATTACHMENT(S), each entry given as an artifact or addendum title and its description (p. 7) [AP].

### Section III and the appendix compared (pp. 6–7, 9–10)

The appendix restates practices 1–4 and their sub-items in the same words as Section III, with one difference: practice 4 reads "The software producer employed automated tools or comparable processes that check for security vulnerabilities" [V] in the appendix (p. 10), where Section III has "employs" (p. 7). The appendix has no row for the further attestation to notify agencies (pp. 9–10) [AP].

## Part VII: The appendix mapping (pp. 9–10)

"The minimum requirements within the Secure Software Attestation Form address requirements put forth in E.O. 14028 subsection" [V] (4)(e). "A mapping to specific SSDF practices and tasks is provided for reference purposes." [V] (p. 9). The table's headed columns are Attestation Requirements, Related E.O. 14028 Subsection, and Related SSDF Practices and Tasks; between the last two sits a fourth column with no heading and no entries (p. 9; the empty column shows in the page image, not the tape) [AP].

The mapping as printed, with codes in their printed form (row 2 prints "PO 1.1", "PW 7.1", "PW 8.1" and "RV 1.1" without the dot):

## Part VIII: The burden statement (p. 8)

The public reporting burden is estimated at 3 hours and 20 minutes per response, including time for reviewing instructions, searching data sources, gathering and maintaining the data needed, and completing and reviewing the collection of information (p. 8) [AP]. "An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number and expiration date." [V] (p. 8). The OMB control number assigned to the collection is 1670-0052, which expires on 03/31/2027 (p. 8) [AP]. Comments on the burden estimate or any other aspect of the collection, including suggestions for reducing the burden, go to DHS/CISA at CSCRM@cisa.dhs.gov, marked "ATTN: PRA 1670-0052 Secure Software Self-Attestation Common Form" [V] (p. 8).

## Connections the author makes in the text

- Executive Order 14028, "Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity": cited as authority for the collection; as having required NIST guidance on practices that enhance the security of the software supply chain (Section 4(e), footnote 1) and the OMB Director to ensure agency compliance with it; subsection (4)(e) is what the minimum requirements address, mapped by subsection in the appendix [BT] (pp. 1, 2, 9–10).
- OMB Memorandum M-22-18 (September 14, 2022), as amended by M-23-16 (June 9, 2023): cited as the requirement that producers attest before agencies use their software, as the source of the scope, and as the minimum requirements the form fulfils [BT] (pp. 1–4).
- NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF), SP 800-218, https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/ssdf: cited as the framework the practices derive from, and by practice and task code in the appendix [BT] (pp. 2, 6, 9–10).
- NIST Software Supply Chain Security Guidance (footnote 3 URL, as the tape gives it: https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2022/02/04/software-supply-chain-security-guidanceunder-EO-14028-section-4e.pdf): with the SSDF, "NIST Guidance", which a 3PAO's assessment baseline must use [BT] (pp. 2, 4, 7).
- FISMA (Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014): cited for agencies' duty to protect information and information systems, and for the OMB Director's authority over standards [BT] (p. 2).
- 44 U.S.C. § 3554: cited as authority for the collection [BT] (p. 1).
- 18 U.S.C. § 1001: cited for willfully false or misleading information [BT] (p. 1).
- DHS/ALL-002 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Mailing and Other List System, 73 FR 71659: cited for DHS's routine uses [BT] (p. 1).
- FedRAMP: cited for certifying a 3PAO [BT] (pp. 4, 7).
- Paperwork Reduction Act: cited for agencies' responsibility for agency-specific additions [BT] (p. 3).
- OMB guidance: cited for agencies' responsibility to request an extension or waiver [BT] (p. 4).

PDF metadata: title "Secure Software Development Attestation Form Instructions", subject "Software Development Attestation", author "Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency"; XMP create date 2024-04-23T12:30:06-04:00, modify date 2024-04-26T11:52:35-04:00. The tape `sources/converted/cisa-secure-software-attestation-form.md` (483 lines, 2,767 words) is the text layer extracted with Poppler `pdftotext -layout`. Post-conversion check: 10 form feeds; footers run 1–10; the end is present (the appendix table closes on p. 10); no truncation marker; about 277 words a page, inside the protocol's 250–400 range.

**Page anchors.** Page breaks in the tape: p. 2 begins at line 52, p. 3 at 109, p. 4 at 162, p. 5 at 204, p. 6 at 254, p. 7 at 307, p. 8 at 361, p. 9 at 384, p. 10 at 436. Section III item 1d runs across the p. 6–7 break (lines 296–312, with the footer and header between); its full wording also appears unbroken in the appendix (p. 9, lines 420–425).

**The appendix table.** In the layout tape the table's three columns interleave line by line (lines 396–478), so in rows 2–4 the line order alone does not show which code list belongs to which requirement. The row assignment in Part VII was confirmed from the PDF with pdfplumber's table extraction: practice 1's parent row and its sub-items 1a–1f are separate rows, and practice 4 with 4a–4c is one cell against 4e(iv) and one code list. The SSDF codes were read from the tape and agree with that extraction.

**Form fields not in the tape.** The text layer shows Section I's checkboxes as "[ ]" but shows no other field. A pypdf listing of the AcroForm fields gives: on p. 3, two checkboxes for the submission route (tooltips "Select the provided URL" and "Local PDF Instructions"); on p. 5, the six Section I checkboxes, seven rows of product name, version number and date fields, and the first Section II producer fields; on p. 6, the remaining producer fields and the primary-contact fields; on p. 7, a checkbox beside the further attestation to notify agencies, a digital-signature field for the CEO or designee, Date Signed, Name and Title fields, and a checkbox beside the 3PAO statement. No field or checkbox sits beside practices 1–4 or their sub-items, and ATTACHMENT(S) has no field. These facts come from the field list, not the tape.

**Variants kept as printed.** Practice 4 reads "employs" in Section III (p. 7) and "employed" in the appendix (p. 10). The second out-of-scope category reads "Open-source software that is freely and directly obtained by a Federal agency" on p. 3 and "Open source software that is freely and directly obtained directly by a Federal agency" on p. 5. Row 2 of the appendix prints four codes without the dot. The appendix names the form "Secure Software Attestation Form" (p. 9) and the burden statement "Secure Software Self-Attestation Common Form" (p. 8). The signature field's tooltip spells "Designess" (field list only). Footnote 3's URL is recorded as the tape gives it, joined across a line break. Line-end hyphens in the tape ("good-" / "faith", "third-" / "party", "M-" / "22-18") are layout, joined in quotations.

**Dates.** The document prints no issue date; the OMB expiration date 03/31/2027 is printed on every page. The date in the example file name (20230124) belongs to the example. The release date of the form is not stated in the document; the creation date above is from the PDF metadata.

**Licence and scope.** The document states no copyright, licence or reuse terms in its text. Its XMP metadata carries no copyright notice and sets `xmpRights:Marked` to False. The licence recorded above (US federal government work, 17 U.S.C. § 105) is the operator's determination. Scope is `open`.

**What this reference does not carry.** The text of the SSDF practices and tasks, which the form cites by code only; anything from E.O. 14028, M-22-18, M-23-16, FISMA or the NIST documents beyond what the form states; anything from CISA's web page for the form or the online form at softwaresecurity.cisa.gov.

**What the form does not state.** It gives no content, format or timeline for a POA&M, no definition of "consistent use", and no date by which an attestation is due (pp. 1–10).
